quantity.c:
QUANTITY, signifies whatsoever is capable of any sort of ■'Estimation or Mensuration, and which being compared with another Thing of the same nature, may be said] to bo. greater or less than, equal or unequal to it. '■ Quantity

au a Quantity may have these four Divisions. 1. Natural Quantity, is what Nature furnishes us with in Matter and its Extension, and in the Powers and Forces of Natural Bodies; such as Gravity, Motion* Light, Heat, Cold, Rarity and Density, (Fe. 2. Moral Quantity, which depend on the Manners of even, and the Free Determination of their Wills; as the Prizes and Values ot Things, Dignity and Power, Good and Evil, Merit and Demerit, Rewards and Punishments, (Fe. z. Notional Quantity, arising from the Operation of the Understanding only ; such as the Largeness or Narrowness ot the Mind’s Capacity, and bf its Conceptions : In Logick, Vnlvcrsnh, Pr.cdicAments, and all such Terms: In Grammar, the Quantity and Meajhe ot Syllables, Accents, Tones, &c. 4. Transcendental Quantity, as Duration, the Continuation of any Beings Existence, 1 ime, (Fe. Quantity is divided also into Continued and Discrete, which see. The QUANTITY of Matter in any Body, is it’s Measure arising from the joint consideration ot it’s Magnitude aud Density : As it a Body twice as Dense, and rake up twice as much space as another, it will be four times as great. And this Quantity' of Matter is best discoverable by the Weight of Bodies, which Mr. Is. Newton found by his nice Experiments on Pendulums, so exactly proportional to the Matter of Bodies. Newton. Princip. The QUANTITY of Motion in any Body, is it’s Measure arising from the joint consideration of the Quantity of Matter in, and the Velocity of the Motion of that Body. For the Motion of any whole is the Sum or Aggregate of the Motion, in ail the several Parts : And tho’ in a Body twice as great as another, moved with an equal Velocity it will be double; but if the Velocity be double also, the Quantity of the Motion will be Quadruple. Newton. Priticip. In Philosophical Trtnsabfidm, Numb. 195. is an Account By 'thte Learned Captain Halhjt> ot the several Species, or Kinds of Infinite Quantity. Where he pie ves, That besides Infinite Length, and Infinite Area, in which there are great Varieties. There arc also no less than three forts of Infinite Solidity. See Infinite Quantities.
